Prompt :
Create a premium professional character reference sheet / production model sheet using the uploaded REFERENCE IMAGE as the ONLY identity reference for the MAIN SUBJECT.

REFERENCE & IDENTITY LOCK:
Use the uploaded reference image as the single source of truth for the subject's identity and appearance.

Preserve the exact:
- Facial identity
- Facial structure
- Skin tone
- Eye shape and natural eye color
- Eyebrows
- Nose
- Lips
- Jawline
- Hairstyle
- Hairline
- Hair texture and natural color
- Age appearance
- Body proportions
- Physique
- Distinctive facial features
- Overall recognizable appearance

The subject may be MALE or FEMALE.

If the reference is male, keep the subject male.
If the reference is female, keep the subject female.

Do NOT change, beautify, feminize, masculinize, or reinterpret the person's identity.

CHARACTER SHEET PURPOSE:
Create a clean professional visual reference sheet that can be used for:
- AI image generation
- AI video generation
- Character consistency
- Animation
- Storyboarding
- Film production
- Fashion visualization
- 3D character development

LAYOUT:
Create one clean, organized professional character sheet on a neutral light studio background.

Divide the composition into clearly arranged sections.

SECTION 1 — FULL BODY VIEWS:
Show the SAME PERSON in multiple full-body views:

1. FRONT VIEW
2. BACK VIEW
3. LEFT SIDE PROFILE
4. RIGHT SIDE PROFILE
5. THREE-QUARTER FRONT VIEW
6. THREE-QUARTER BACK VIEW

Keep the subject standing naturally with consistent proportions.

All views must represent EXACTLY the same person.

SECTION 2 — FACE REFERENCE:
Create a detailed facial reference grid showing the SAME PERSON from multiple angles:

- Front-facing portrait
- Left profile
- Right profile
- Left three-quarter view
- Right three-quarter view
- Slightly elevated facial angle
- Slightly lowered facial angle
- Neutral expression close-up

Preserve facial proportions exactly across every angle.

SECTION 3 — HAIR REFERENCE:
Clearly show the subject's hairstyle from:
- Front
- Left
- Right
- Back

Preserve exact hair length, texture, volume, color, hairline, and natural styling.

SECTION 4 — OUTFIT:
Dress the subject in a clean, simple, premium outfit suitable for professional character reference.

The outfit should remain identical across every full-body view.

If the reference image contains a distinctive outfit that is important to the character, preserve its key design, colors, materials, and silhouette.

If no specific outfit is required, use a simple neutral contemporary outfit that clearly shows the body's natural proportions.

POSE & BODY CONSISTENCY:
All views must maintain:
- Identical height
- Identical body proportions
- Identical physique
- Identical shoulder width
- Identical facial proportions
- Identical hairstyle
- Identical clothing
- Identical accessories

Do not generate different versions of the person.

FACIAL EXPRESSION:
Keep the primary facial references neutral and relaxed.

Do not exaggerate expressions.

The face must remain highly recognizable in every panel.

CAMERA:
Professional studio photography.
Straight-on camera alignment for front/back views.
True profile alignment for side views.
Consistent focal length and camera distance.
No extreme wide-angle distortion.

Use the same lighting setup across every panel.

LIGHTING:
Soft professional studio lighting.
Even illumination.
Minimal harsh shadows.
Neutral white/gray background.
Clean photographic presentation.

VISUAL STYLE:
Ultra-photorealistic.
Professional character design sheet.
High-end fashion model reference photography.
Production-ready visual reference.
Extremely detailed facial features.
Realistic skin texture.
Realistic hair strands.
Natural anatomy.
Accurate body proportions.
Sharp facial details.
Clean studio presentation.

CONSISTENCY PRIORITY:
Every panel must show the EXACT SAME PERSON.

The face must remain consistent across all angles.

Do not create separate identities for different panels.

Do not alter facial proportions between views.

Do not change hairstyle between views.

Do not change body proportions between views.

Do not change clothing between views.

REFERENCE IMAGE RULE:
The uploaded reference image controls the subject's identity and recognizable appearance.

Do NOT copy the original reference image's background unless specifically requested.

Reconstruct the person cleanly inside the professional studio character-sheet environment.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS:
No identity change.
No different person.
No face variation.
No face blending.
No gender change.
No age change.
No facial beautification that changes identity.
No different hairstyle.
No different hair color.
No inconsistent body proportions.
No distorted face.
No asymmetrical anatomy caused by generation errors.
No extra limbs.
No extra fingers.
No malformed hands.
No duplicated body parts.
No inconsistent clothing.
No different person in different panels.
No cartoon style.
No CGI appearance.
No plastic skin.
No dramatic background.
No clutter.
No text.
No watermark.
No logo.

FINAL OUTPUT:
Create a polished professional character/model reference sheet with multiple views arranged neatly on a single canvas.

The result should look like an actual professional production reference sheet prepared for a film, fashion campaign, animation, or AI character-consistency workflow.

RESOLUTION LOCK:
Generate the final image in 16K resolution — 15360 × 8640 pixels (≈132.7 million pixels), landscape composition.

🎉 Five papers accepted at NeurIPS 2026!

Excited to share our work across protein design, RNA design and evaluation, efficient LLM agents, and multimodal safet
Here’s what we explored 👇

🧬 1 | Grounding protein generation in physics
<Equivariant Force Field Calibration for Flow-based Protein Design>

Generative models can produce protein structures quickly—but physical plausibility remains a critical challenge.

This work combines differentiable force-field guidance with consistency-based training to calibrate flow models toward low-energy, sterically valid conformations. Across full-atom generation and peptide binder modeling, we improve physical plausibility and geometric stability while enabling sampling with very few steps.

🧪 2 | Learning RNA design preferences from physical feedback
<Pareto Preference Optimization for Structure- and Stability-Aware RNA Inverse Folding>

RNA design requires satisfying several objectives together: structural fidelity, local accuracy, and thermodynamic stability. Optimizing one metric can create shortcuts that undermine the others.

We introduce RiboPO, a preference optimization framework that constructs preferences through Pareto comparisons, uses structural gates to guard against compositional reward hacking, and fine-tunes an RNA inverse-folding model using DPO.

📄 Earlier preprint:
https://t.co/vaCxwPzlid

💻 Code (anonymous review repository):
https://t.co/QGvWWAzJGt

🔍 3 | Testing whether RNA design scores deserve our trust
<Multi-Oracle Agreement Reveals the Limits of Self-Consistency Evaluation in RNA Design>

What happens when the predictor used to optimize a sequence is also used to evaluate it? Across approximately 11,000 RNA designs, we find that 78.1% of designs from single-objective optimization pass one predictor yet fail another. Ensemble-based methods reduce this disagreement substantially.

We introduce ACCORD, an evaluation workflow that combines independent predictors and calibrates their disagreement against experimental chemical-mapping data.

📄 Paper:
https://t.co/9aaIHcUNnj

💻 Code (anonymous review repository):
https://t.co/ABGhHfbEMd

⚡ 4 | Making LLM agents more efficient by changing how they act
<Latent Action Reparameterization for Efficient Agent Inference>

Agent inference cost depends on both the cost of each decision and the number of decisions required.

LAR learns compact, executable latent actions from recurring patterns in agent trajectories. This shortens the effective decision horizon, reducing action tokens and inference time while maintaining or improving task success across the evaluated benchmarks.

📄 Paper:
https://t.co/UneHr0ue8q
💻 Code:
https://t.co/Oq6qq9jxH6

🛡️ 5 | Understanding the safety implications of thinking with images
<When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?>

As vision-language models increasingly reason through visual operations and external tools, their inference pipelines become part of the safety question.

Across the evaluated models, explicit image-tool interaction reduces jailbreak success by around 30% relative on average. Representation analyses and activation interventions support an account in which tool invocation shifts hidden states toward a safety-relevant direction.

📄 Paper:
https://t.co/bCsVQQIS5E

Huge thanks to my coauthors, advisors, and collaborators for making this work possible!
#NeurIPS2026 #AIforScience #ProteinDesign #RNADesign #LLMAgents

第1003期 小路和你读AI论文。今日4篇高质量论文。

1. 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗦𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝗦𝗙𝗧 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝘀 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸（《带采样的微调：SFT 比你想的更会学》）

链接：https://t.co/QXVXbqz5hu

作者背景：Aayush Karan, Sitan Chen, Yilun Du, Harvard

不改损失，用 MCMC 把离策略专家轨迹逐步改写成更接近参考模型的在策略分布，SFT 在泛化与遗忘上就能比肩强在策略后训练。实验覆盖科学技能、数学推理和开放式专长。采样本身可以当作后训练原语，这会动摇"保能力必须上 RL"的默认做法，做后训练的人值得细看。

2. 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗙𝗶𝘁: 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹-𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗧𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀（《找到合适的搭配：跨 Agent 任务的模型与 Harness 交互》）

链接：https://t.co/txmUWsp8E5

作者背景：Yixuan Li, Bo An 等

模型、harness 与任务必须放在一起评，强模型和厂商自有脚手架都不会稳定领先。66 组配置横跨 OpenHands、DeepSeek Harness、PI、openJiuwen 与三项命令行 agent 基准。Terminal-Bench 4 上，Claude 在 OpenHands 中领先 GPT 7.94 分，在 PI 中落后 30.16 分，五个模型里有四个的最优 harness 随基准改变。作者发布了适配器、评测代码和 6,204 条轨迹，部署 agent 的人可以直接拿来做选型证据。

3. 𝗛𝗶𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘂𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀（《分层连续扩散语言模型》）

链接：https://t.co/dC0fv3j4PU

作者背景：Alexander Schwing（UIUC）等

让连续潜变量成为唯一持续生成状态，token 每步读出并回馈，以缓解离散扩散并行解码时的独立采样断裂。训练目标来自 token 似然的变分界，同规模下在 Sudoku、Countdown 和 LM1B 上优于离散与连续扩散基线。做扩散语言模型的人可以看看它是否真正保住了并行解码中的 token 依赖。

4. 𝗘𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆 𝗔𝗯𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗜𝘀 𝗮 𝗗𝗼𝘀𝗲: 𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘄𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗦𝗲𝗹𝗳-𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗿（《每次消融都是一剂药：反权重与"自修复"的假象》）

链接：https://t.co/IzLv2zqidD

消融后看似补偿的响应，多半来自干预前就存在的反权重，它们随对比强度作仿射响应，与临时自我修复无关。在事实判决任务上，Gemma、Qwen、LLaMA、Mistral 的 81 个下游方向中有 68 个服从该仿射律。GPT-2 Small 的 IOI 电路里，干预能触及的 10 个头有 7 个符合，且全是反权重，斜率还能由固定权重预先估计。做机制可解释性的人可以拿它校准对自修复的判断。

几乎所有 reward model 都在做同一个简化：把人类偏好压成一个分数。

但真实的人类反馈往往不是一个点——同一个回答，不同人可以给出不同、甚至互相冲突的判断。把多峰偏好硬压成标量，模型学到的只是"平均值"，而不是"人们到底怎么想"。

清华 THUNLP 的新工作 DRM（Diffusion Reward Model）换了个问法：能不能让奖励模型学人类偏好的分布？

做法很干净——把 reward modeling 重新表述为对 p(r | x, y) 的条件密度估计：在冻结的 LLM encoder 之上，用轻量 Diffusion Transformer 从高斯噪声去噪出奖励向量。不对输出分布做任何参数假设，多峰结构自然被表示出来。
一个架构同时吃多属性回归和成对偏好数据；推理时采 N 个样本就是经验奖励分布，可以聚合成标量、方差或分位数。

结果（五个基准）： • 在数据与 backbone 对齐下不弱于基线 • 训练规模相对小，仍能与大得多的判别式 / 分布式 / 生成式 RM 抗衡 • 常规 head 把分布坍缩成一个点时，它能恢复出多峰结构

更实用的是下游：用不确定性做拒绝采样、用 LCB 聚合——而且直接拿 DRM 当 RLHF 训练时的 reward，策略表现更好。这就不只是"更细的评估指标"，而是能直接改善训练。

一句话：奖励不该是一个点，而是一个分布。

via @HBX_hbx

We are releasing Kalaido-open, our suite of models for image generation and editing, along with the ProductConsistency benchmark.

All models and the benchmark are available here: https://t.co/mdBPS2wX3f

Kalaido Qwen Edit is a general-purpose image editor, fine-tuned from Qwen-Image-Edit with reinforcement learning. It improves general editing, background preservation and instruction following. On ImgEdit, it scores 4.71 in our comparison, ahead of GPT-5.1 (4.60) and Qwen-Image-Edit (4.52).

Kalaido Qwen Image is our text-to-image model, fine-tuned from Qwen-Image-2512 with reinforcement learning. It improves text rendering, prompt adherence and visual quality. On OneIG Text, it scores 0.979, ahead of Qwen-Image (0.891) and GPT-Image-1 (0.857).

In the benchmark chart, "Kalaido-open" refers to the suite: generation benchmarks reflect Kalaido Qwen Image, and ImgEdit reflects Kalaido Qwen Edit.

The ProductConsistency benchmark accompanies our CVPR paper, which targets text preservation in product advertisement images.
